what_it_does: When multiple processors (CPUs, GPUs) coordinate on shared data, coherence protocols ensure all processors see consistent memory. In write-through protocols, the source processor must route every write through the central directory for consistency, creating round-trip communication delays. CORD relocates this responsibility to the directory itself — it accumulates writes locally and enforces consistency without contacting the source processor. This reduces latency, interconnect traffic, and power for producer-consumer AI and machine-learning workloads running across multiple processors.
